summary: postinstall reconnaissance beacon exfiltrates host, user, network, and credential-shaped env inventory to hardcoded bare IP
details: The package declares a postinstall script that runs dist/recon.js on npm install. recon.js harvests hostname, username, SUDO_USER, home directory, cwd, all local IPv4 network interface addresses (including internal), DNS domain (via dnsdomainname), CI indicators, the full list of process.env variable names, and a subset of those names filtered by a credential-keyword regex covering AWS, GCP, GOOGLE, AZURE, NPM, NODE_AUTH, DOCKER, KUBE, VAULT, TOKEN, SECRET, KEY, PASS, CRED, GITHUB, GITLAB, and SSH patterns. The collected JSON payload is POSTed over plaintext HTTP to hardcoded bare IP 138.68.108.20:80/cb, which is not the package's documented publisher endpoint. The combination — automatic execution at install time, host/user/internal-network reconnaissance, credential-surface inventory, and exfiltration to an unattributed bare-IP endpoint over cleartext HTTP — is a supply-chain reconnaissance beacon that maps installer machines and identifies which hosts hold AWS, NPM, GitHub, and SSH secrets for follow-up targeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
